diet.text: Frogs and tadpoles, fish, lizards, earthworms and crayfish

overview.text: The Western Ribbon Snake is a slender, harmless garter snake that lives near water, from the central United States through Mexico to Costa Rica.

identification.text: Very slender with a long tail (about a third of its length). Black, brown or olive with three light stripes; the lips are white and unmarked, standing out against the dark head.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The central and southern United States, eastern Mexico and Central America south to central Costa Rica.

habitat.text: Many habitats, usually not far from water, from sea level to nearly 2,500 m.

diet.text: Small animals: earthworms, crayfish, lizards, fish, frogs and tadpoles.

recognise.text: Three light stripes on a dark, very slim body.
